title: A tale of london
summary: A collection of short fantasy pieces by Lord Dunsany (Edward Plunkett, eighteenth Baron Dunsany), gathering tales of dreamlike and uncanny settings. The opening story, "A Tale of London," is a hasheesh-eater's rapturous description of an imagined London of ebony houses, golden balconies and white sand streets, told to a Sultan. Other pieces include "Bethmoora," a meditation on a desolate desert city abandoned after a mysterious message; "Charon," in which the ferryman of the dead grows weary as the shades arrive in ever greater numbers; "How the Enemy Came to Thlunrana," about a prophesied doom befalling a sinister house of wizardry; and "The Exiles Club," in which deposed kings dine in a London basement among their salvaged heirlooms. The later tales are more whimsical and satirical, including a narrator's bargain for a trivial fear and an account of the secret tale told by the Company of Milkmen. Written in a lyrical, archaic style with rich imagery, the collection draws on myth, Eastern romance and the odd humour of ordinary London life.
